sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Greater burdock is a branching biennial, commonly about 75–150 cm tall, native across temperate Eurasia and introduced elsewhere. Its broad heart-shaped leaves can reach about 50 cm; purple flower heads form hooked burs that attach to passing animals.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The first-year taproot is cultivated and eaten as gobo, especially in East Asia; young leaf stalks are also used as food. The roots become tough as the plant flowers. Distinguish this species from lesser burdock, A. minus, whose heads are smaller and usually more closely clustered on shorter stalks.

sections.title: Image note
sections.text: The plate's large leaves and burred heads match burdock; exact dimensions vary with age and growing conditions.
